label: Census and Vital Statistics — mastery test (unseen; refreshed 12 November 2026)

items.stem: The first synchronous census of India was conducted in:
items.explanation: 1881 was the first synchronous census — the whole country enumerated at one reference moment — and censuses have been decennial since. 1872 is the first census of India, but it was taken at different times in different parts of the country, and 1948 is the year of the Census Act.
items.check: 1872 first census, 1881 first synchronous, 1948 the Act, 1949 the permanent organisation. The question asks which was synchronous.

items.stem: The census of India is conducted by:
options: The Registrar General of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
items.explanation: The Registrar General of India, who is ex-officio Census Commissioner, in the Ministry of Home Affairs. This is the one part of Unit X that does not sit with MoSPI, and the examiner knows that the rest of the module trains you to answer MoSPI by reflex.

items.stem: The infant mortality rate is defined as deaths under one year of age per:
items.explanation: IMR is per 1,000 live births. The crude birth and death rates use mid-year population, the maternal mortality ratio uses 1,00,000 live births, and 1,000 women aged 15-49 is the denominator of the general fertility rate — every wrong option is a real denominator borrowed from a neighbouring measure.

items.stem: Registration of births and deaths in India is compulsory under:
options: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
items.explanation: The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 made registration compulsory throughout India, and was amended in 2023. The Census Act, 1948 and the Census Rules, 1990 govern the census, and the Collection of Statistics Act, 2008 governs the statistical surveys of MoSPI — three different instruments for three different operations.

items.stem: The Sample Registration System is based on:
items.explanation: Two independent records of the same events — continuous recording by a part-time local enumerator and a half-yearly retrospective survey by a supervisor — are matched, and the mismatches are verified in the field. That matching is what lets the SRS catch events a single register would miss.

items.stem: A birth or death must be reported to the registrar within how many days of the event?
items.explanation: 21 days, at the place where the event occurred, with penalties rising for delay. The figure of 30 days belongs elsewhere in the same law — it is the window for filing an appeal with the District Registrar or Chief Registrar.
items.check: 21 days to report; 30 days to appeal; 90 days for the appeal to be decided. The question asks about reporting.

items.stem: For the four poll-bound States/areas named in ORGI's 5 September 2026 notification, the self-enumeration window is:
items.explanation: ORGI's schedule for Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and non-snow-bound Uttarakhand provides self-enumeration 16-30 November, Population Enumeration 1 December 2026-4 January 2027 and revisional round 5-9 January 2027.
items.check: Self-enumeration is in November; door-to-door enumeration spans December and early January; the revisional round follows immediately.

items.stem: Which statement about the Population Enumeration schedule of Census 2027 is correct?
options: All States and UTs use one identical fieldwork window in February 2027
Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and non-snow-bound Uttarakhand have a separate notified schedule
The self-enumeration window for the four poll-bound areas is 1-15 November 2026
The revisional round for the four poll-bound areas ends on 30 November 2026
items.explanation: ORGI's current portal lists a separate schedule for these four States/areas: self-enumeration 16-30 November 2026, Population Enumeration 1 December 2026-4 January 2027 and revisional round 5-9 January 2027. Fieldwork dates must not be confused with the national reference moment.
items.check: Identify which of the schedule stages the question asks about.

items.stem: Consider the following statements about amendments to the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.
items.explanation: A is correct: the 2023 amendment provides for the national database and birth-certificate provisions. B is incorrect: the delayed-registration magistrate change belongs to the 2026 amendment, not the 2023 Act. C is correct: ORGI's current page describes the parent Act as amended in both 2023 and 2026. D is correct: for information furnished more than two years after the event, the 2026 amendment requires an order of a Judicial Magistrate First Class.
statements: The 2023 amendment provides for a national database of registered births and deaths under the Registrar General.
The delayed-registration magistrate change made in 2026 was already part of the 2023 amendment.
ORGI's current Vital Statistics Division page identifies amendments in both 2023 and 2026.
For information furnished more than two years after the event, the 2026 change requires an order of a Judicial Magistrate First Class.

A.why: The 2023 amendment provides for the national database under the Registrar General.

B.why: The delayed-registration magistrate change belongs to the 2026 amendment, not the 2023 amendment.

C.why: ORGI's current page identifies amendments in 2023 and 2026.

D.why: The 2026 amendment provides for a Judicial Magistrate First Class order after two years.

items.stem: The Sample Registration System began full-scale operations in:
items.explanation: A pilot ran in selected states in 1964-65 and full-scale operations began in 1969-70. 1951 is the year the Office of the Registrar General was set up, and both 1964-65 and 1969-70 are correct answers to different questions — which is why the question specifies full scale.

items.stem: The age-specific fertility rates per 1,000 women for a population, in five-year groups from 15-19 to 45-49, sum to 340. The total fertility rate is:
items.explanation: With five-year age groups, TFR = 5 × Σ ASFR with the rates expressed per woman: 5 × 340/1000 = 1.70. The figure 3.40 comes from forgetting the factor of 5 and dividing by 100 instead, 0.34 from omitting the factor of 5 altogether, and 17.00 from dividing by 100 — all three are the standard slips.
items.check: A TFR is a number of children, so it must be a few units. Anything above about 8 or below about 0.5 should be rechecked.

items.stem: Match the system or measure in List I with its description in List II.
items.explanation: The census is the decennial complete count that supplies population denominators; the CRS is the continuous legal registration of individual events; the SRS is the continuous sample survey that produces India's vital rates; and the NRR is the measure for which a value of 1 is exact replacement. Each wrong option moves at least two pairs, so the mapping has to be checked rather than inferred from one recognised entry.
items.check: Anchor on the two you are certain of — the census and the NRR — then the two registration systems separate by sample versus complete.
pairs: I. Continuous legal registration of individual events
II. A value of 1 means exact replacement
III. Decennial complete count supplying population denominators
IV. Continuous sample survey producing India's vital rates

items.stem: India reports its sex ratio at birth as 917 for 2021-23. The figure is expressed as:
options: Female births as a percentage of all births
items.explanation: India's convention is females per 1,000 males, so 917 means 917 girls for every 1,000 boys — below the biological value of roughly 952. Much international work reports the ratio the other way round, as males per 100 females, where the natural value is about 105; a figure near 1,050 in a question is using that other convention.

items.stem: If the crude birth rate is 18.4 and the crude death rate is 6.4 per 1,000 population, the natural growth rate is:
items.explanation: The natural growth rate is simply CBR minus CDR: 18.4 − 6.4 = 12.0 per 1,000. It is called natural because it excludes migration. The option 24.8 adds the two rates and 2.88 divides them, both of which are meaningless here.
items.check: Natural growth is a difference, not a sum or a ratio, and it excludes migration entirely.

items.stem: According to ORGI's national Vital Statistics based on CRS report for 2024, released in July 2026, birth registration completeness was:
items.explanation: ORGI reports birth-registration completeness of 99.1% in 2024, up from 82.4% in 2011. Death registration was 99.4% in 2024, up from 66.4% in 2011. The 97.2% value belongs to the earlier 2023 CRS report and is deliberately date-labelled here as a distractor. These are registration-completeness percentages, not demographic rates such as CBR or IMR.
items.check: Attach the reference year: 2024 birth registration 99.1%; death registration 99.4%.

items.stem: Consider the following statements about the Sample Registration System.
items.explanation: A, C and D hold: it is run by the Registrar General of India, it covered 8,839 sampling units and over 8.8 million people by 2023, and it is sized so that the infant mortality rate can be estimated with a relative standard error below 15%. B is false — the SRS is an administrative survey resting on no statute, unlike the census and civil registration, each of which has its own Act.
statements: It is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General of India.
It operates under a statute of its own.
By 2023 it covered 8,839 sampling units and over 8.8 million people.
Its sample is designed so that IMR has a relative standard error below 15%.

A.why: The same body that takes the census and oversees civil registration.

B.why: No statute. The Census Act 1948 covers the census and the RBD Act 1969 registration; the SRS is administrative.

C.why: And the supervisor updates each unit's population by age, sex and marital status.

D.why: The design criterion was set on a named indicator rather than by convenience.

items.stem: A population has a total fertility rate of 2.00 and a sex ratio at birth of 900 females per 1,000 males. Taking the probability that a newborn girl survives to the mean age of childbearing as 0.90, the net reproduction rate is approximately:
items.explanation: The proportion of births that are female is 900/(900+1000) = 0.4737, not 900/1000. So GRR = 2.00 × 0.4737 = 0.947 and NRR = 0.947 × 0.90 = 0.853. The option 0.95 is the GRR, offered because candidates stop one step early, and 1.80 comes from multiplying TFR by the survival probability and forgetting the daughters step altogether.
items.check: NRR must be below GRR, which must be a little under half of TFR. 0.85 < 0.95 < 1.00 passes all three checks.

items.stem: A statement reads: 'India's total fertility rate of 1.9 is below the replacement level, so India's population is now declining.' What is wrong with it?
options: The replacement level is 1.9, so the TFR is not below it
A below-replacement TFR is consistent with a growing population because of the age structure
The TFR of 1.9 refers to urban India only
Nothing is wrong; the statement is accurate
items.explanation: Replacement level is about 2.1, so the first half of the statement is right. The flaw is the inference: a young age structure means a large number of women are entering their childbearing years, so births continue to exceed deaths for decades after fertility falls below replacement. This is population momentum, and it is why TFR and the growth rate can point in apparently opposite directions.

items.stem: A district's registered births for last year are divided by its estimated population to give a birth rate. Which systems supplied the two quantities, and where does the greater uncertainty lie?
options: Numerator from the SRS, denominator from the CRS; the numerator is weaker
Numerator from the CRS, denominator projected from the census; the denominator is weaker
Both from the CRS; the two are equally reliable
Numerator from the census, denominator from the SRS; the denominator is weaker
items.explanation: A count of registered events for a named district can only come from the CRS, because the SRS is a sample and publishes no district estimates and the census does not count births. The population must be projected forward from Census 2011, since the 2021 round was postponed — so the denominator carries sixteen years of projection error, including unmeasured migration, and that dominates the uncertainty in the rate.

items.stem: India's sex ratio at birth for 2021-23 is 917, against a biological value of roughly 952 on the same convention. The state figures range from 974 to 868. The statistically correct reading is that:
options: The gap is within the sampling error of the SRS
The biological value differs across Indian states
The three-year averaging has biased the national figure downwards
The shortfall is systematic, and the state variation must reflect behaviour rather than biology
items.explanation: A biological constant cannot vary by state, so a range from 974 to 868 locates the variation in behaviour. Nor is the gap sampling noise: the SRS covers over 8.8 million people and the figure is averaged over three years precisely to damp year-to-year variation, which reduces noise rather than introducing bias. This is the one indicator in the set that does not fit a pattern of steady improvement.
